chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Isma'il ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And do not make Allah an excuse on your oaths,' he said: 'It is when you are invited for reconciliation between two people, that you say: 'Upon me is an oath that I will not do it.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'And do not make Allah an excuse on your oaths' mean in the context of reconciliation?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the prohibition in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:224 targets using oaths as a pretext to avoid *Sulh* (reconciliation), a highly meritorious act in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the scholarly distinction between merely swearing an oath and actively employing it to obstruct social harmony, thereby emphasizing the priority of peacemaking over rigid adherence to one's own verbal commitments.
